title: Assistant Teaching Professor, Business & Economics
description:
About Salve Regina University:

Salve Regina University, ranked as one of the most transformative
colleges in the United States by Money Magazine, is a comprehensive
Catholic University located in the scenic coastal community of
Newport, Rhode Island. The University's commitment to academic
success and personal discovery extends beyond its historic campus
into a dynamic world where the application of higher thinking and
skill are most valued. Salve Regina offers bachelor's and master's
degree programs, graduate certificates, and doctoral programs in
humanities, international relations and nursing. Enrollment
includes more than 2,600 undergraduate and graduate students from
across the U.S. and around the world.

Job Description:

Salve Regina University provides a student-centered teaching
environment grounded in values of compassion, service, and academic
excellence. Faculty have the opportunity to work closely with
students, contribute meaningfully to curriculum and departmental
initiatives, and help students connect their education with
purposeful careers and lives of service. The Teaching Professor
track recognizes the central importance of excellent teaching,
mentorship, and service to the academic community.

The Jean and David W. Wallace Department of Business and Economics
serves a large and diverse population of undergraduate students
across business and economics programs. The Department emphasizes
strong teaching, experiential learning, close faculty-student
engagement, career preparation, and ethical leadership. Faculty
work collaboratively to provide students with rigorous academic
foundations while helping them connect classroom learning to
professional and civic life.

The Jean and David W. Wallace Department of Business and Economics
at Salve Regina University invites applications for a full-time
Assistant Teaching Professor of Economics beginning August 2027.
This is a non-tenure-track appointment on the University's Teaching
Professor track, a faculty pathway centered on excellence in
teaching, student advising and mentorship, and meaningful service
to the Department and University.

The successful candidate will teach a 4/4 course load. Teaching
assignments are expected to include introductory and intermediate
microeconomics and macroeconomics, with additional courses assigned
according to departmental needs and the candidate's areas of
expertise. We seek an engaged, student-centered educator who can
make economics accessible, relevant, and rigorous for Economics
majors as well as students from business and other
disciplines.

The position is grounded in Salve Regina University's Mercy
Mission, with its emphasis on educating the whole person, ethical
leadership, service, and respect for the dignity of all
people.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Teach a 4/4 undergraduate course load, primarily in
introductory and intermediate microeconomics and
macroeconomics.
Teach additional economics courses based on departmental needs
and the candidate's expertise.
Design and deliver engaging, rigorous, and student-centered
instruction that connects economic theory with contemporary
business, policy, and societal issues.
Advise and mentor undergraduate students in their academic and
professional development.
Contribute to departmental curriculum development, assessment,
and continuous improvement initiatives.
Participate in appropriate departmental and University service
activities.
Maintain currency in the discipline through professional
development, applied scholarship, or other appropriate forms of
continued engagement.

Requirements:

Required Qualifications:

Master's degree in Economics or a closely related field from an
accredited institution.
Demonstrated ability to teach economics effectively at the
undergraduate level or evidence of strong potential for effective
college-level teaching.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills and a commitment
to student success.
Commitment to contributing to a collaborative academic
department and to Salve Regina University's Mercy Mission.

Preferred Qualifications

Ph.D. or other appropriate terminal degree in Economics or a
closely related field.
Prior college-level teaching experience, particularly in
introductory and/or intermediate microeconomics and
macroeconomics.
Evidence of teaching effectiveness.
Ability to contribute to multiple areas of the economics
curriculum.
Experience teaching applied economics, quantitative methods,
data analysis, business economics, public policy, or related
courses.
Experience advising, mentoring, or supporting undergraduate
students from a range of academic backgrounds.

Additional Information:

Salve Regina University offers generous benefits to eligible
employees including (waiting periods apply):

health, dental and vision coverage available on the first of
the month following date of hire
403(b) retirement plan through TIAA with employee and employer
contributions as well as access to advising services
long-term disability coverage
employer-paid life and AD&D insurance
up to 100% free tuition at Salve for eligible employees and
qualified dependents
robust wellness program and free access to the on-campus
Fitness Center

Other available benefits include:

supplemental life insurance for employees and dependents
supplemental insurance coverage through Aflac
Tuition Exchange scholarship program. Application available for
qualified dependents of eligible employees working full-time
discounted pet insurance through ASPCA
student loan forgiveness assistance program (SAVI)
employee Assistance Program through Health Advocate
flexible spending health and dependent care accounts
health savings accounts
529 collegebound saver program
paid parental leave and adoption assistance

For more detailed information on Salve's benefits, visit https://salve.edu/human-resources/benefits .

Salve Regina University strives to cultivate belonging values
through diversity, equity inclusion in order to foster a welcoming
culture for our staff, faculty and students, as well as the wider
community. Salve Regina University embraces all people with grace.
No matter the path traveled to get here, the University
acknowledges that many identities will intersect. Salve Regina
belongs to all in its community.

Application Instructions:

Applicants must apply online by providing the following
materials:

Cover letter describing the candidate's qualifications,
teaching experience and philosophy, and interest in the
position.
Curriculum vitae or resume.
Names and contact information for three professional
references.
Evidence of teaching effectiveness, if available.

Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled. Pre-employment background checks and
reference checks are required of successful candidates. Salve
Regina University participates in E-verify.
